name: caddy
description: Fast and extensible multi-platform HTTP/1-2-3 web server with automatic HTTPS
one_liner: A web server program that automatically sets up the security certificate, the padlock icon in your browser, for any website, instead of someone having to configure that by hand.
buyer: A DevOps engineer or small hosting provider who wants to run many websites securely without manually managing SSL certificates for each one.
business_use_cases: A small managed-hosting provider uses it to auto-provision HTTPS for every customer site it hosts, cutting support tickets about broken certificates.
An internal platform team standardizes on it so every internal tool gets HTTPS and routing configured automatically.
A freelance sysadmin offers 'secure hosting setup' as a quick paid service for small business websites, using Caddy to handle the hard parts.

money_ideas.idea: Offer paid managed-hosting or 'secure website setup' services built on top of it for small businesses.
Sell enterprise support and consulting contracts for companies running it at scale, a well-trodden open-source infrastructure playbook.

steal_this: This weekend, package a one-click 'secure static site hosting' service for freelancers and small businesses using Caddy under the hood.
